# Pagination

Figma: [06g. Pagination](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-937) · Family: 06 Navigation · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-15

Moves through a long, ordered set page by page. Two atoms - PaginationItem and PaginationArrow - compose into numbered, compact, and table layouts that drop into any card, toolbar, or table footer, across LTR + RTL.

### PaginationItem

A 36px page number cell (or the ellipsis) used to build Pagination; current page gets the brand fill.

Level: atom · Part of: Pagination

Use when:
- Inside Pagination or a custom pagination row; Label holds the page number or the ellipsis

Don't use when:
- Carousel position dots: use PageIndicator
- Step numbers: use StepIndicator

Accessibility: aria-label 'Page 3', aria-current=page on the current item; Western digits per Syntropy number rules.

### PaginationArrow

Previous or next 36px button in Pagination, disabled on the first and last page instead of hidden.

Level: atom · Part of: Pagination

Use when:
- Inside Pagination, or alone for compact prev/next paging

Don't use when:
- Back navigation: use BackButton
- Carousel arrows on media: use IconButton

Accessibility: aria-label Previous page / Next page; disabled state uses aria-disabled; chevrons mirror in RTL.

### Pagination

Splits long ordered result sets into pages with prev/next and page numbers, in numbered, compact (Page X of Y) and table footer (rows per page + range) layouts. Main use is back-office tables of deals, investors and transactions.

Level: organism · Contains: PaginationItem, PaginationArrow, Select

Use when:
- Back-office Table footers (Type=table with rows-per-page Select and '1-10 of 200')
- Long ordered lists where users need an exact page or total (Type=numbered)
- Narrow cards, toolbars or mobile (Type=compact)

Don't use when:
- Continuous exploratory feeds such as updates: use infinite scroll or a Load more Button
- Lists that fit on one screen: omit it
- Carousel position: use PageIndicator

Accessibility: nav aria-label=Pagination; current page aria-current; keep a single line; use Western digits (0-9) even in RTL, overriding the page guide's Arabic-Indic note.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Type | `type` | variant | numbered, compact, table | numbered |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Pagination breaks a long, ordered result set into pages and lets people jump between them. It trades the effort of a click for predictable position and performance - the user always knows how much is left and can return to an exact page.

### When to use

- Long, ordered lists where position matters - deals, transactions, search results - especially in tables.
- When people need to reach a specific page or know the total count.

### When not to use

- Continuous, exploratory feeds - prefer infinite scroll or a “Load more” button.
- Very short lists that fit on one screen.

### Live preview

### Atomic architecture

Two small, reusable segments compose every layout - so the same pagination drops into a card, a toolbar, or a table footer.

### Atoms

- PaginationItem - a 36px page cell. State default (link), hover, current (brand fill), disabled. Holds a number or the ··· ellipsis via its Label.
- PaginationArrow - a 36px prev/next button. Direction left/right (mirrors per reading direction) × State default · hover · disabled.

### Organism

- Pagination - alternates the atoms into numbered, compact, and table layouts × Direction.

> **Info:** Because the parts are independent, you can assemble any pagination you need - add a page-size Select, swap the numbers for a range, or keep only the arrows - without a new component.

### Anatomy

- Previous arrow - moves back one page; disabled on the first page.
- Page items - the reachable pages; exactly one is current (brand fill).
- Ellipsis (···) - a PaginationItem standing in for the hidden middle pages.
- Next arrow - moves forward one page; disabled on the last page.
- Optional - a range readout (“1–10 of 200”) and a page-size selector for table footers.

### States

Item and arrow states.

default

hover

current

disabled

arrow

arrow · disabled

- default - a reachable page link. hover - subtle fill. current - brand fill + bold, marks the page you are on (not a link).
- disabled - an unreachable page or an edge arrow (first/last) - dimmed and non-interactive.

### Layouts

Three ready compositions of the same two atoms. Pick by context and space.

numbered

Full page numbers with prev/next. The default - for lists and cards where people jump around.

compact

Just arrows + “Page X of Y”. For tight toolbars, mobile, and narrow cards.

table

Range readout + page-size + arrows. For table footers where total and rows-per-page matter.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Order reverses and the prev/next chevrons swap sides with the reading direction.

LTR

Page 1 on the left; prev chevron points left, next points right.

RTL

Page 1 on the right; chevrons mirror; Arabic-Indic numerals where appropriate.

### Behavior

- Exactly one page is current; the current item is not a link.
- Disable Previous on the first page and Next on the last - never hide them (keeps the layout stable).
- Keep ~7 cells visible; collapse the middle to ··· and always show the first and last page.
- Single line, no wrapping - switch to the compact layout before it would wrap.
- In tables, pair with a page-size Select and a “X–Y of N” range so totals are clear.

### Code examples

### HTML · ARIA

```dart
<nav aria-label="Pagination">
  <ul class="pagination">
    <li><a aria-label="Previous page" aria-disabled="true">‹</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1" aria-current="page">1</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=2">2</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=3">3</a></li>
    <li aria-hidden="true">…</li>
    <li><a href="?page=10">10</a></li>
    <li><a aria-label="Next page" href="?page=2">›</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

### Usage - Do and Don’t

Do

Do mark the current page, disable the edge arrows, and always show the first and last page.

Don’t

Don’t make the current page a link or let the row wrap - switch to compact before it would.

Do

Do pair table pagination with a range readout and page-size so totals are clear.

Don’t

Don’t use pagination for a continuous, exploratory feed - use infinite scroll or “Load more”.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Two atoms - PaginationItem and PaginationArrow - compose every layout. To build a custom pagination, lay the atoms in a row; nothing else is needed.

> **Info:** The ellipsis is just a PaginationItem with Label = “···”. For RTL, set numerals to Arabic-Indic (١ ٢ ٣) to match the locale.

> **Warning:** The table layout’s page-size is a real Select (03d) - a compact Select Value chip showing the rows-per-page count; wire its options (10 · 25 · 50 · 100) in code. Arrow chevrons mirror via a flip transform, not a separate icon.
